# Audio

94 tools for Sound Cues, MetaSounds, submixes and buses, sound classes, attenuation and concurrency, modulation, dialogue and subtitles.

Back to the [index](README.md).

## `add_bus_to_mix`

*Additive.*

Adds a USoundControlBus to a USoundControlBusMix asset as a new stage whose target value is default_value, and saves the mix. A bus already in the mix is left unchanged (already_in_mix true, not saved); edit a stage with set_control_bus_mix_stage_value. Returns mix_path, bus_path, bus_count, added, saved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mix_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the USoundControlBusMix |
| `bus_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the USoundControlBus |
| `default_value` | number | no | Target value for the new mix stage (default 1.0) |

**Returns:** `{ mix_path, bus_path, bus_count, added, already_in_mix, saved, default_value }`

## `add_metasound_graph_input`

*Additive.*

Add a graph input of data_type (default Float) to an existing MetaSound Source through the MetaSound builder, inside an undo transaction, then save the asset. Optionally bakes a typed default into the new input; give at most one of default_value, int_value, bool_value or string_value (bool_value wins, then int_value, string_value, default_value). An unregistered data_type or a source that does not load is an error, and so is a default of the wrong JSON type or one data_type takes no literal of, with nothing written. A name already used by an input is left untouched: with the same data_type the call succeeds with added=false and already_exists=true, saves nothing and does not apply a supplied default (note says so; use set_metasound_graph_input_default); with another data_type it is an error. success is false, with save_error, when the save fails (during PIE, for one). Inverse: remove_metasound_graph_input.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the MetaSound Source, as a package path like "/Game/MetaSounds/MS_Example" or an object path like "/Game/MetaSounds/MS_Example.MS_Example" |
| `input_name` | string | yes | Name of the graph input node to add. |
| `data_type` | string | no | Frontend data type: "Float", "Int32", "Bool", "String", "Audio", "Trigger" (optional, default "Float") |
| `default_value` | number | no | Float default baked into the literal, a JSON number (optional) |
| `int_value` | number | no | Int32 default baked into the literal, a whole JSON number (optional, mutually exclusive with other defaults) |
| `bool_value` | boolean | no | Bool default baked into the literal, JSON true or false (optional, mutually exclusive with other defaults) |
| `string_value` | string | no | String default baked into the literal, a JSON string (optional, mutually exclusive with other defaults) |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, input_name: string, data_type: string, added: bool, already_exists?: bool, has_default: bool, note?: string, saved: bool, save_error: string? }`

## `add_metasound_graph_output`

*Additive.*

Add a graph output of data_type (default Audio; others include Float, Int32, Bool, String and Trigger) to an existing MetaSound Source through the MetaSound builder, inside an undo transaction, then save the asset. An unregistered data_type or a source that does not load is an error. A name already used by an output is left untouched: with the same data_type the call succeeds with added=false and already_exists=true and saves nothing; with another data_type it is an error. success is false, with save_error, when the save fails (during PIE, for one). Inverse: remove_metasound_graph_output.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the MetaSound Source. |
| `output_name` | string | yes | Name of the graph output node to add. |
| `data_type` | string | no | Frontend data type for the output node (optional, default "Audio") |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, output_name: string, data_type: string, added: bool, already_exists?: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string? }`

## `add_metasound_interface`

*Additive.*

Adds a registered interface to an existing MetaSound Source's graph.  Obtains a builder for the saved asset via the editor subsystem's FindOrBeginBuilding (the reliable headless path), validates the interface via IsInterfaceRegistered, then calls UMetaSoundBuilderBase::AddInterface (which adds the interface's input/output nodes). The asset is saved after the edit. Inverse: remove_metasound_interface.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the MetaSound Source (e.g. "/Game/MetaSounds/MS_Example" or fully-qualified ".MS_Example"). |
| `interface_name` | string | yes | Name of a registered MetaSound interface to add (required) |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, node_kind: string, interface_name: string, added: bool, saved: bool }`

## `add_metasound_node`

*Destructive.*

Add a real process node to a MetaSound Source graph by its registered class name (e.g. UE/Sine/Audio).  Unlike add_metasound_graph_input (which adds a graph input node), this instantiates a DSP node so you can author a real signal patch headless. Returns the node's GUID (node_id) and its enumerated input/output pins (name + data_type) for follow-up set/connect calls. The asset is saved. NOT idempotent: each call adds a new node instance (delete + recreate the source for a clean run). Wire it with connect_metasound_nodes, connect_metasound_graph_input_to_node or connect_metasound_node_to_graph_output; edges: list_metasound_connections.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the MetaSound Source. |
| `class_namespace` | string | yes | Registered node class namespace, e.g. "UE". |
| `class_name` | string | yes | Registered node class name, e.g. "Sine". |
| `class_variant` | string | no | Optional class variant, e.g. "Audio" (omit for the default/no-variant class). |
| `major_version` | number | no | Optional major version (default 1). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, node_id: string, class_namespace: string, class_name: string, class_variant: string, inputs: [{name,data_type}], outputs: [{name,data_type}], added: bool, saved: bool }`

## `add_modulation_input_to_patch`

*Additive.*

Appends a USoundControlBus as an input of a USoundModulationPatch asset and saves the patch. A bus whose asset name is already among the inputs is skipped (added false, already_present true, not saved). input_name is not stored. Returns patch_path, bus_path, input_count, added, already_present, saved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `patch_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the USoundModulationPatch |
| `bus_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the USoundControlBus to add as an input |
| `input_name` | string | no | Ignored: the engine input struct has no name field, so the value is only written to the log (default empty) |

**Returns:** `{ patch_path, bus_path, input_count, added, already_present, saved }`

## `add_sound_cue_node`

*Additive.*

Append a new node of node_type to the AllNodes of a USoundCue asset, in one undo step, and save the cue; node_id is its index there, the id the other sound cue tools take. node_type is matched without case, and an unknown type or a cue that does not load is an error. The node starts unconnected and is not the cue output: wire it with connect_sound_cue_nodes and make the root with set_sound_cue_first_node. For a WavePlayer, sound_wave_path sets its wave; a wave that does not load is not an error (sound_wave_set=false), and other types ignore it. Each call adds another node (not idempotent). A failed save, as during PIE, makes success false with save_error. Node settings: set_sound_cue_node_properties; read back: get_sound_cue_graph; a new cue: create_sound_cue. Inverse: remove_sound_cue_node.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cue_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the cue, e.g. /Game/SoundCues/SC_Foo |
| `node_type` | string | yes | One of WavePlayer\|Mixer\|Random\|Looping\|Modulator\|Delay\|Concatenator\|Attenuation\|Branch\|DistanceCrossFade\|Doppler\|Enveloper\|GroupControl\|ModulatorContinuous\|Oscillator\|ParamCrossFade\|QualityLevel\|SoundClass\|Switch\|WaveParam (matched without case) |
| `sound_wave_path` | string | no | Optional USoundWave path for WavePlayer nodes only; one that does not load leaves the node without a wave (sound_wave_set false) |

**Returns:** `{ cue_path: string, node_id: int, node_type: string, node_class: string, max_child_nodes: int, child_count: int, sound_wave_set: bool, sound_wave_path: string, node_count: int, saved: bool }`

## `add_soundfield_effect_to_submix`

*Additive.*

Append a new effect of a concrete USoundfieldEffectBase class to a USoundfieldSubmix effect chain and save it; an addition succeeds only when the submix reaches disk. A class already in the chain is skipped (added false, already_present true, not saved). When no concrete subclass is loaded (stock UE 5.8 ships none) nothing changes and the call fails, with added false and a note.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `submix_path` | string | yes | Full path to the USoundfieldSubmix (required). |
| `effect_class_name` | string | yes | Full class path of a concrete USoundfieldEffectBase subclass, e.g. "/Script/MyAudioPlugin.MySoundfieldEffect"; it is looked up with no outer, so a bare class name does not resolve |

**Returns:** `{ submix_path, effect_path, effect_class, chain_length, added, already_present, saved, note? }`

## `add_submix_effect_to_chain`

*Additive.*

Append one effect preset to the end of a USoundSubmix's effect chain and save the submix. effect_preset_path wins: that existing USoundEffectSubmixPreset asset is appended by reference. Otherwise a new preset of effect_preset_class, or, when neither is given, of a concrete class found by reflection (SubmixEffectDynamicsProcessorPreset when it is loaded), is created inside the submix's own package under a unique &lt;Submix>_Effect name; resolved_from says which of the three ran. Every call appends another entry, duplicates included. A submix or preset that does not load, or a class that is not a concrete preset subclass, is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. Read the chain with get_submix_effect_chain and tune an entry with set_submix_effect_settings; a soundfield submix takes add_soundfield_effect_to_submix. Inverse: remove_submix_effect_from_chain.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `submix_path` | string | yes | Full content path of the target USoundSubmix |
| `effect_preset_path` | string | no | Optional existing USoundEffectSubmixPreset asset to append by reference; wins over effect_preset_class |
| `effect_preset_class` | string | no | Optional concrete USoundEffectSubmixPreset subclass (short name or path) to instantiate in the submix's package; with neither preset param a class is picked by reflection |

**Returns:** `{ submix_path: string, effect_name: string, effect_class: string, resolved_from: string, effect_added: bool, chain_length: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_subtitle_cue`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Append one cue (text, start_offset, duration, duration_type, subtitle_type, priority, comment) to the Subtitles list of a USubtitleAssetUserData asset loaded by content path, in one undo step, then save it. Idempotent: a cue equal to it in text, duration_type, duration, start_offset, priority and subtitle_type -- comment is not compared -- is a success with already_existed=true, saved=false and that cue's cue_index, nothing added or saved. Defaults: start_offset 0, duration 3 s, duration_type use_duration_property, subtitle_type subtitle, priority 1. An unknown duration_type or subtitle_type, or an asset that does not load, is an error; so is a failed save, after which the cue is already in memory. Edit a cue (text or timing) with set_subtitle_cue and list them with list_subtitle_cues; the inverse is remove_subtitle_cue. Create the asset with create_subtitles_asset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_path` | string | yes | Content path of the USubtitleAssetUserData asset. |
| `text` | string | yes | The subtitle text (required). |
| `start_offset` | number | no | Initial delay in seconds before the subtitle is visible (default 0). |
| `duration` | number | no | Display duration in seconds (default 3). |
| `duration_type` | string | no | "use_sound_duration" or "use_duration_property" (default "use_duration_property"). |
| `subtitle_type` | string | no | "subtitle", "closed_caption", or "audio_description" (default "subtitle"). |
| `priority` | number | no | Subtitle priority; higher values play instead of lower (default 1). |
| `comment` | string | no | Editor-only author comment (default ""). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, cue_index: int, text: string, success: bool, already_existed: bool, cue_count: int, saved: bool, message: string? }`

## `connect_metasound_graph_input_to_node`

*Destructive.*

Wire the graph input graph_input_name of a MetaSound Source to the input to_input_name of node to_node_id, in one undo step, then save the asset -- how a parameter (a Float input "Frequency") drives a node pin. Same rules as connect_metasound_nodes: matching data types, an input already fed is re-fed (replaced=true), the same edge already there changes nothing (already_connected=true), and an unknown graph input, node or pin is an error with nothing changed. Read back: list_metasound_connections; inverse: disconnect_metasound_nodes on the node input. Graph input to graph output: connect_metasound_graph_input_to_output.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the MetaSound Source. |
| `graph_input_name` | string | yes | Name of the graph input (get_metasound_info lists them). |
| `to_node_id` | string | yes | GUID of the node whose input receives the edge. |
| `to_input_name` | string | yes | Name of that node's input pin. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, graph_input_name: string, to_node_id: string, to_input_name: string, from_data_type: string, to_data_type: string, connected: bool, already_connected: bool, replaced: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string?, note: string? }`

## `connect_metasound_graph_input_to_output`

*Destructive.*

Connects a graph input node's output to a graph output node's input.  Resolves the source handle from a graph INPUT node by name (FindGraphInputNode -> the input node's output handle) and the destination handle from a graph OUTPUT node by name (FindGraphOutputNode -> the output node's input handle), then calls UMetaSoundBuilderBase::ConnectNodes and verifies via NodesAreConnected. The connection is real where the two data types match (e.g. a Float graph input connected to a Float graph output). Saves the asset. Graph input to a node: connect_metasound_graph_input_to_node; edges: list_metasound_connections.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the MetaSound Source. |
| `from_node_output_name` | string | yes | Name of the graph INPUT to use as the connection source. |
| `to_node_input_name` | string | yes | Name of the graph OUTPUT to use as the connection target. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, from_node_output_name: string, to_node_input_name: string, from_data_type: string, to_data_type: string, connected: bool, result: string, verified: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string? }`

## `connect_metasound_node_to_graph_output`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Connect a concrete node's output pin to a named graph output, completing a signal patch (e.g. Sine.Audio -> the source's audio output).  Uses ConnectNodeOutputToGraphOutput (idempotent: replaces any existing edge). Reports the honest EMetaSoundBuilderResult. Node to node: connect_metasound_nodes; edges: list_metasound_connections.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the MetaSound Source. |
| `node_id` | string | yes | GUID of the source node (from add_metasound_node). |
| `node_output_name` | string | yes | Name of the node's output pin (e.g. "Audio"). |
| `graph_output_name` | string | yes | Name of the target graph output (discover via get_metasound_info). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, node_id: string, node_output_name: string, graph_output_name: string, connected: bool, result: string, saved: bool }`

## `connect_metasound_nodes`

*Destructive.*

Wire the output from_output_name of node from_node_id to the input to_input_name of node to_node_id in a MetaSound Source graph, in one undo step, then save the asset -- the node-to-node edge a patch needs (Sine.Audio -> ADSR.In). Node ids come from add_metasound_node or list_metasound_nodes, pin names from their inputs/outputs. The two pins must carry the same data type. An input takes one edge, so an input already fed from elsewhere is re-fed (replaced=true); the same edge already there changes and saves nothing (already_connected=true). A bad id, an unknown pin or a type mismatch is an error and nothing changes. Read back: list_metasound_connections; inverse: disconnect_metasound_nodes. A graph input as the source: connect_metasound_graph_input_to_node; a graph output as the target: connect_metasound_node_to_graph_output.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the MetaSound Source. |
| `from_node_id` | string | yes | GUID of the node whose output feeds the edge. |
| `from_output_name` | string | yes | Name of that node's output pin (e.g. "Audio"). |
| `to_node_id` | string | yes | GUID of the node whose input receives the edge. |
| `to_input_name` | string | yes | Name of that node's input pin (e.g. "In"). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, from_node_id: string, from_output_name: string, to_node_id: string, to_input_name: string, from_data_type: string, to_data_type: string, connected: bool, already_connected: bool, replaced: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string?, note: string? }`

## `connect_sound_cue_nodes`

*Destructive.*

Link the node child_node_id into an input slot of the node parent_node_id in a USoundCue asset (ids from add_sound_cue_node or get_sound_cue_graph), in one undo step, then save the cue. With input_index that slot is overwritten even when it holds another child (missing slots up to it are added empty); without it the first empty slot is used, or a new one is appended. A cue that does not load, an id out of range, a parent that takes no children (a WavePlayer), an input_index outside [0, max_child_nodes), a full parent, or a cycle (a node into itself or into a node feeding it) is an error, with nothing changed. Duplicate links are allowed: a repeat without input_index adds the child again. A failed save, as during PIE, makes success false with save_error. Inverse: disconnect_sound_cue_nodes; cue output: set_sound_cue_first_node; read back: get_sound_cue_graph.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cue_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the cue |
| `parent_node_id` | number | yes | node_id of the upstream node with inputs (its index in the cue AllNodes) |
| `child_node_id` | number | yes | node_id of the node to feed into the parent |
| `input_index` | number | no | Optional zero-based target slot; an occupied slot is overwritten. Omitted: the first empty slot, else a new slot appended |

**Returns:** `{ cue_path: string, parent_node_id: int, child_node_id: int, input_index: int, parent_class: string, child_class: string, parent_child_count: int, connected: bool, saved: bool }`

## `create_audio_bus`

*Destructive.*

Creates a UAudioBus asset at package_path/name and saves it, or loads the one already there (already_exists true) and saves it again; another asset class at that path is an error. channels, when given, sets the channel layout, overwriting an existing bus's layout; when omitted a new bus gets Stereo and an existing one keeps its own. An invalid channels value is refused before any asset is created or loaded. Change the layout later with set_audio_bus_channels and read it with get_audio_bus; create_sound_source_bus makes a source bus that plays this bus's audio.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Name of the new Audio Bus asset |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content path, defaults to /Game/Audio |
| `channels` | string | no | EAudioBusChannels: 'Mono' \| 'Stereo' (default) \| 'Quad' \| 'FiveDotOne' \| 'SevenDotOne'. The default applies to a new bus only. |

**Returns:** `{ name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, asset_class: string, channels: string, channels_int: int, num_channels: int, applied_channels: bool (this call wrote the layout: channels given, or the Stereo default on a new bus), created: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `create_control_bus`

*Additive.*

Creates a USoundControlBus asset at package_path/bus_name, or loads the one already there, and saves it. initial_value is only echoed back as value, never written to the bus; push a runtime value with set_control_bus_value. Returns bus_path, default_value, created, already_existed, saved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bus_name` | string | yes | Name of the control bus (e.g. "Bus_Volume") |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/MCP) |
| `initial_value` | number | no | Number echoed back as value in the reply; it is not stored on the bus (default 1.0) |

**Returns:** `{ bus_path, bus_name, value, default_value, created, already_existed, saved }`

## `create_control_bus_mix`

*Additive.*

Creates a USoundControlBusMix asset at package_path/mix_name, or loads the one already there, and saves it. A new mix has no stages; add buses with add_bus_to_mix. Returns mix_path, mix_name, bus_count (its stage count), created, saved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mix_name` | string | yes | Name of the control bus mix asset |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/MCP) |

**Returns:** `{ mix_path, mix_name, bus_count, created, saved }`

## `create_metasound_preset`

*Additive.*

Creates a MetaSound preset from an existing source or patch asset.  Uses UMetaSoundBuilderSubsystem::CreateSourcePresetBuilder (or CreatePatchPresetBuilder) to create a transient preset builder referencing the source, then BuildToAsset to persist it as a new /Game asset. A preset of that type already at the path is returned unchanged with already_exists=true, saved=false and preset_type read from its class, nothing saved; an asset of another class there (a MetaSound of the other type included) is an error and nothing is created.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `preset_name` | string | yes | Name of the new MetaSound preset asset. |
| `source_asset_path` | string | yes | Content path of the existing MetaSound source/patch to use as the preset's template. |
| `package_path` | string | no | Destination /Game folder (default /Game/MetaSounds). |
| `preset_type` | string | no | "source" (default) or "patch". |

**Returns:** `{ preset_path: string, preset_type: string, success: bool, saved: bool, already_exists: bool, message: string? }`

## `create_metasound_source`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create a UMetaSoundSource asset at package_path/name (default folder /Game/MetaSounds): a one-shot source graph pre-wired with the source interface (OnPlay input, OnFinished output, one audio output per channel), built by the MetaSound builder subsystem and written with BuildToAsset, then saved; no dialog, no undo step. Idempotent: a MetaSound Source already there is returned unchanged with already_exists=true, created=false and saved=false, nothing saved. output_format is mono, stereo, quad, 5.1 or 7.1; anything else is an error and nothing is created. The reply's output_format is read from the source, also for an existing one, whose own format is reported and left as it is. An invalid package name or a failed build is an error; a failed save gives success false with save_error. Next: add_metasound_node, add_metasound_interface; inspect: get_metasound_info; inverse: delete_asset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Name of the MetaSound Source asset to create. |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target /Game package path (optional, default "/Game/MetaSounds") |
| `output_format` | string | no | Output audio format: "mono", "stereo", "quad", "5.1", or "7.1" (optional, default "mono") |

**Returns:** `{ source_name: string, asset_path: string, created: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool, output_format: string, class_name: string, input_count: number, output_count: number, save_error: string?, message: string? }`

## `create_modulation_generator`

*Destructive.*

Creates a modulation generator asset of class LFO, ADEnvelope or EnvelopeFollower at generator_path (or package_path/generator_name), with engine default settings, and saves it; for an LFO it also writes the given waveform, frequency, amplitude, offset and phase (looping on), on a new LFO or overwriting those fields of an existing one. An existing generator with no LFO field given is returned untouched with its own class (not saved). LFO fields with another generator_class or on an existing generator of another class, and an unknown waveform, are errors. Returns generator_path, generator_name, generator_class, settings as stored, created, already_existed, updated, saved. Configure the other classes with set_modulation_generator_settings.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `generator_class` | string | yes | Concrete class name (case-insensitive). One of: LFO, ADEnvelope, EnvelopeFollower |
| `generator_path` | string | no | Full asset path (e.g. /Game/MyGame/Gen_LFO). Optional when generator_name is given. |
| `generator_name` | string | no | Optional asset name, used with package_path when generator_path is absent. |
| `package_path` | string | no | Optional folder for generator_name (default /Game/MCP); ignored when generator_path is given. |
| `waveform` | string | no | Optional, LFO only: shape, case-insensitive: Sine, UpSaw, DownSaw, Square, Triangle, Exponential, Random (RandomSampleHold). Any other value is an error. |
| `frequency` | number | no | Optional, LFO only: frequency in Hz (engine default 1.0). |
| `amplitude` | number | no | Optional, LFO only: amplitude (engine default 1.0). |
| `offset` | number | no | Optional, LFO only: output offset (engine default 0.0). |
| `phase` | number | no | Optional, LFO only: starting phase (engine default 0.0). |

**Returns:** `{ generator_path, generator_name, generator_class, settings: {...}, created, already_existed, updated, saved }`

## `create_modulation_parameter`

*Additive.*

Creates a USoundModulationParameter asset of the chosen concrete class at parameter_path and saves it. An existing parameter there is returned untouched with its real class (not saved). Returns parameter_path, parameter_name, parameter_class, created, already_existed, saved. Tune it with set_modulation_parameter_settings.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `parameter_path` | string | yes | Full asset path (e.g. /Game/MyGame/Param_Volume); the package path is the directory portion and the leaf becomes the asset name |
| `parameter_class` | string | yes | Concrete class name (case-insensitive). One of: Volume, Frequency, LPFrequency, HPFrequency, Bipolar, Additive, Scaled; the engine spellings LPFFrequency and HPFFrequency are accepted too. |

**Returns:** `{ parameter_path, parameter_name, parameter_class, created, already_existed, saved }`

## `create_sound_attenuation`

*Additive.*

Create a USoundAttenuation asset at package_path/name, or load the one already there, then force bAttenuate on, apply the optional falloff_distance and sphere radius, and save it (re-running edits the existing asset). Returns the values read back; set_properties edits every other field.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Name of the new Sound Attenuation asset |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content path, defaults to /Game/Audio |
| `falloff_distance` | number | no | FalloffDistance in Unreal units (cm): how far beyond the inner shape the volume fades out. Unchanged when omitted. |
| `radius` | number | no | Inner sphere radius in Unreal units (cm); sets the shape to Sphere and AttenuationShapeExtents to (radius, 0, 0). Unchanged when omitted. |

**Returns:** `{ name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, asset_class: string, attenuate: bool, falloff_distance: number, radius: number, shape_extent_x: number, shape_extent_y: number, shape_extent_z: number, applied_falloff_distance: bool, applied_radius: bool, created: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool }`

## `create_sound_class`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Create a USoundClass asset at package_path/name (package_path defaults to /Game/Audio) and save it. A sound class already at that path is loaded instead (already_exists true, created false) and the volume and pitch you pass overwrite its values before it is saved again; omitted ones keep their current values, the engine defaults on a new class. Idempotent. The reply reads volume and pitch back from the asset, and applied_volume / applied_pitch say which were written. An invalid path, or an asset of another class there, is an error; a failed save (for example during PIE) makes success false with saved=false and save_error. Edit the other properties with set_properties, read them with get_sound_class_properties, and wire the hierarchy with set_sound_class_parent.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Name of the new Sound Class asset |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content path, defaults to /Game/Audio |
| `volume` | number | no | Optional Volume multiplier on FSoundClassProperties; also written to a class that already exists, unchanged when omitted |
| `pitch` | number | no | Optional Pitch multiplier on FSoundClassProperties; also written to a class that already exists, unchanged when omitted |

**Returns:** `{ name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, asset_class: string, volume: number, pitch: number, applied_volume: bool, applied_pitch: bool, created: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `create_sound_concurrency`

*Additive.*

Create a USoundConcurrency asset at package_path/name, or load the one already there, optionally set MaxCount, and save it. Returns max_count read back, created, already_exists and saved; set_properties edits the other concurrency settings.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Name of the new Sound Concurrency asset |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content path, defaults to /Game/Audio |
| `max_count` | number | no | Most sounds of this group that play at once (MaxCount); values below 1 become 1 and fractions are truncated. Unchanged when omitted. |

**Returns:** `{ name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, asset_class: string, max_count: int, applied_max_count: bool, created: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool }`

## `create_sound_cue`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create an empty USoundCue asset (no nodes and no first node, so it plays nothing yet) at package_path/name and save it. Idempotent: a sound cue already at that path is returned unchanged with created=false and already_existed=true, and nothing is saved; an asset of another class there is an error and nothing is written. Not an undo step. Build the graph next with add_sound_cue_node, connect_sound_cue_nodes and set_sound_cue_first_node, and read it back with get_sound_cue_graph; cue_path is the path those tools take. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and the new cue left in memory.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name, e.g. 'SC_Footsteps'; package_path/name must form a valid long package name. |
| `package_path` | string | no | Content folder as a long package path, e.g. '/Game/Audio/Cues' (default /Game/SoundCues); trailing slashes are ignored. |

**Returns:** `{ name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, cue_path: string, created: bool, already_existed: bool, node_count: int, saved: bool, message: string }`

## `create_sound_mix`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Create a USoundMix asset at package_path/name (package_path defaults to /Game/Audio) and save it; a sound mix already there is loaded instead (already_exists true) and the eq_enabled and duration you pass overwrite its values before it is saved. Omitted fields keep their current values; the reply reads eq_enabled and duration back from the asset. An invalid path, or an asset of another class there, is an error; a failed save is an error with the change kept in memory. Idempotent. Add per-class volume and pitch adjusters with set_sound_mix_class_override; create the classes with create_sound_class.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Name of the new Sound Mix asset |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content path, defaults to /Game/Audio |
| `eq_enabled` | boolean | no | Optional bool, sets USoundMix::bApplyEQ (whether to apply the EQ effect). Left at the asset default when absent. |
| `duration` | number | no | Optional float, sets USoundMix::Duration in seconds (negative means applied until another mix is set). Left at the asset default when absent. |

**Returns:** `{ name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, asset_class: string, eq_enabled: bool, duration: number, applied_eq_enabled: bool, applied_duration: bool, created: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool }`

## `create_sound_modulation_patch`

*Additive.*

Creates a USoundModulationPatch asset at package_path/patch_name with no inputs or output, bypassed by default (bBypass true), and saves it; a patch already there is returned untouched, not re-saved. Returns patch_path, bBypass, input_count, output_parameter_path, created, already_existed, saved. Fill it with add_modulation_input_to_patch and set_modulation_patch_output_parameter.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `patch_name` | string | yes | Name of the modulation patch asset (e.g. "Patch_Volume") |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/MCP) |

**Returns:** `{ patch_path, patch_name, bBypass, input_count, output_parameter_path, created, already_existed, saved }`

## `create_sound_source_bus`

*Destructive.*

Creates a USoundSourceBus asset at package_path/name, or loads the one already there, writes its routing fields and saves it; another asset class at the path is an error. source_bus_channels and duration, when omitted, take the defaults (Stereo, 1.0 s) on a new asset and keep their value on an existing one, whose fields the given values overwrite. Every value is validated before any asset is created or loaded, so an invalid one leaves nothing behind. audio_bus_path, when given, must load as a UAudioBus and becomes the bus whose audio this source bus plays; when omitted that field is left as is. Edit later with set_sound_source_bus_audio_bus or set_sound_source_bus_send_info; read with get_sound_source_bus.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Name of the new Sound Source Bus asset |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content path, defaults to /Game/Audio |
| `source_bus_channels` | string | no | ESourceBusChannels: 'Mono' \| 'Stereo' (default). USoundSourceBus inherits only Mono/Stereo. The default applies to a new asset only. |
| `duration` | number | no | Duration in seconds, at least 0 (0.0 means indefinite); a negative value is an error. Default 1.0 on a new asset only. |
| `audio_bus_path` | string | no | Optional full content path of a UAudioBus to assign as the AudioBus return. |

**Returns:** `{ name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, asset_class: string, source_bus_channels: string, duration: float, audio_bus_path: string, audio_bus_class: string, applied_channels: bool, applied_duration: bool (each true when this call wrote the field: given, or the default on a new asset), applied_audio_bus: bool, created: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `create_sound_submix`

*Additive.*

Create an empty USoundSubmix asset at package_path/name, or load the one already there, and save it. Returns asset_path, created, already_exists and saved; add effects with add_submix_effect_to_chain and read them with get_submix_effect_chain.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Name of the new Sound Submix asset |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content path, defaults to /Game/Audio |

**Returns:** `{ name: string, package_path: string, asset_path: string, asset_class: string, created: bool, already_exists: bool, saved: bool }`

## `create_soundfield_submix`

*Additive.*

Create a USoundfieldSubmix asset at submix_path and save it, with its default encoding format and an empty effect chain; a new one succeeds only when it reaches disk. An existing one there is returned unchanged and not re-saved (already_existed true, saved false). Returns soundfield_encoding_format, effect_chain_length and saved; inspect it with get_soundfield_submix_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `submix_path` | string | yes | Full asset path like "/Game/Audio/MySFSubmix" (required). |

**Returns:** `{ submix_path, asset_path, soundfield_encoding_format, encoding_settings_class, created, already_existed, saved }`

## `create_subtitles_asset`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Create a USubtitleAssetUserData asset -- the engine's subtitle authoring asset, a list of timed cues -- at package_path/name (default folder /Game/MCP), register it and save it; no undo step. Idempotent: a subtitles asset already at that path is returned unchanged with already_existed=true, saved=false, a message and its cue_count, nothing saved. An invalid package name, or a name taken by an asset of another class, is an error, and so is a failed save of the new asset -- refused while PIE runs, under a read-only root, or a read-only file -- which leaves it unsaved in memory. Fill it with add_subtitle_cue and read it with list_subtitle_cues; delete it with delete_asset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Name of the new subtitles asset. |
| `package_path` | string | no | Destination /Game folder (default /Game/MCP). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, success: bool, already_existed: bool, cue_count: int, saved: bool, message: string? }`

## `disconnect_metasound_graph_input_from_output`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Disconnects a graph input node's output from a graph output node's input (inverse of connect_metasound_graph_input_to_output).  Resolves the source handle from a graph INPUT node by name (FindGraphInputNode -> the input node's output handle) and the destination handle from a graph OUTPUT node by name (FindGraphOutputNode -> the output node's input handle), then queries NodesAreConnected first: if the edge is already absent it returns already_disconnected without error (idempotent), otherwise it calls UMetaSoundBuilderBase::DisconnectNodes and reports the result. Saves the asset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the MetaSound Source. |
| `from_node_output_name` | string | yes | Name of the graph INPUT whose output is the connection source. |
| `to_node_input_name` | string | yes | Name of the graph OUTPUT whose input is the connection target. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, from_node_output_name: string, to_node_input_name: string, from_data_type: string, to_data_type: string, disconnected: bool, already_disconnected: bool, result: string, saved: bool, save_error: string?, note: string? }`

## `disconnect_metasound_node_from_graph_output`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Disconnects whatever node output currently drives a named graph output, clearing the edge (inverse of connect_metasound_node_to_graph_output).  Resolves the graph output node's input handle by name (FindGraphOutputNode) and queries NodeInputIsConnected first: if the input is already unconnected it returns already_disconnected without error (idempotent), otherwise it calls UMetaSoundBuilderBase::DisconnectNodeInput and reports the result. Saves the asset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the MetaSound Source. |
| `graph_output_name` | string | yes | Name of the target graph output to disconnect (discover via get_metasound_info). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, graph_output_name: string, data_type: string, disconnected: bool, already_disconnected: bool, result: string, saved: bool, save_error: string? }`

## `disconnect_metasound_nodes`

*Destructive.*

Drop the edge that feeds the input to_input_name of node to_node_id in a MetaSound Source graph, whatever drives it -- another node's output or a graph input -- in one undo step, then save the asset. Inverse of connect_metasound_nodes and connect_metasound_graph_input_to_node: an input takes one edge, so the input names it. The reply says which output fed it (from_node_id, from_output_name) and re-reads the input. An input with no edge is an honest no-op (disconnected=false, already_disconnected=true, nothing saved); a bad node id or an unknown pin is an error. Read first: list_metasound_connections; a graph output's edge: disconnect_metasound_node_from_graph_output.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the MetaSound Source. |
| `to_node_id` | string | yes | GUID of the node whose input loses its edge. |
| `to_input_name` | string | yes | Name of that node's input pin. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, to_node_id: string, to_input_name: string, from_node_id: string?, from_node_name: string?, from_output_name: string?, disconnected: bool, already_disconnected: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string? }`

## `disconnect_sound_cue_nodes`

*Destructive.*

Clear a wired child out of a parent node's input slot (inverse of connect_sound_cue_nodes)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cue_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the cue |
| `parent_node_id` | number | yes | node_id of the upstream node whose input slot is cleared |
| `child_node_id` | number | no | Optional node_id of the wired child; its slot is located via IndexOfByKey |
| `input_index` | number | no | Optional slot to clear directly; supply this OR child_node_id |

**Returns:** `{ cue_path: string, parent_node_id: int, child_node_id: int, input_index: int, parent_class: string, child_class: string, parent_child_count: int, disconnected: bool, already_disconnected: bool, saved: bool }`

## `get_audio_bus`

*Read-only.*

Read the channel layout of a UAudioBus asset: channels (Mono, Stereo, Quad, FivePointOne or SevenPointOne), channels_int and num_channels. Read-only. is_active is always false because no audio device is queried. Change the layout with set_audio_bus_channels.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bus_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAudioBus, e.g. "/Game/Audio/AB_Music". |

**Returns:** `{ bus_path: string, asset_class: string, channels: string, channels_int: int, num_channels: int, is_active: bool (always false: headless — no audio device) }`

## `get_audio_component_properties`

*Read-only.*

Read an editor-level audio component by object name: volume, pitch, active state, transform, sound and its duration, and the attenuation really applied (override, else asset, else sound). Use it for these derived values; get_component_properties reads raw UPROPERTYs. Every audio component of every actor is searched, the name compared without case. Component names are unique only per actor (every AmbientSound's is AudioComponent0), so a name that several actors carry is an error listing the owners unless actor_name (object name, not label) picks one; an actor_name that names no actor, or whose actor has no component of that name, is an error too. Read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio_component_name` | string | yes | Object name of the audio component to query (e.g. "AudioComponent0"), compared without case against EVERY audio component of every actor in the editor world. |
| `actor_name` | string | no | Optional object name (not label) of the actor that owns the component, compared without case. Needed when several actors own an audio component of that name (every AmbientSound's is AudioComponent0): without it that is an error listing the owners. An actor_name that names no actor, or whose actor has no such component, is an error. |

**Returns:** `{ audio_component_name: string, audio_component_found: bool, audio_component_message: string, component_class: string, component_type: string, audio_volume: number, audio_pitch: number, audio_enabled: bool (IsActive), audio_auto_activate: bool, audio_mobility: string, audio_position: { x, y, z }, audio_rotation: { pitch, yaw, roll }, audio_scale: { x, y, z } (component world transform), audio_sound_name: string, audio_sound_class: string, audio_sound_duration: number, audio_sound_path: string ("None" with no sound), audio_sound_is_sound_wave: bool, audio_sound_is_sound_cue: bool, audio_3d_enabled: bool (bAllowSpatialization), audio_3d_attenuation_radius: number (shape extent X), audio_3d_attenuation_falloff: number (both 0 with no attenuation applied), audio_3d_attenuation_cone_angle: number, audio_3d_attenuation_cone_feather: number (cone shape only, else 0), audio_owner_name: string, audio_owner_class: string, audio_owner_path: string, audio_owner_position: { x, y, z }, audio_owner_rotation: { pitch, yaw, roll }, audio_level: string, audio_world: string }`

## `get_audio_settings`

*Read-only.*

Survey audio in the editor: a census of the first audio component of every actor in the editor world (even while PIE runs), with each one's volume, pitch and playing, looping and spatialized state, the counts and volume and pitch statistics, and the main audio device's state (audio_enabled, max channels, mixer loaded). Read-only; no parameters. Several fields are not measured: audio_quality comes from the channel count (64+ High, under 32 Low), audio_api is the platform's default backend, reverb and occlusion always read true, sample rate and buffer size are fixed defaults, and the recommendations and complexity score are heuristics. For the project's audio settings use get_project_settings_value; for one component in depth, get_audio_component_properties.

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ audio_settings_found: bool, audio_quality: string, audio_api: string, audio_enabled: bool, audio_mode: string, world_name?: string, audio_component_count: int, active_audio_component_count: int, spatialized_audio_component_count: int, average_volume: number, max_volume: number, max_pitch: number, engine_version: string, platform_name: string, audio_max_channels: int, audio_3d_enabled: bool, audio_reverb_enabled: bool, audio_occlusion_enabled: bool, audio_recommendations: [string], audio_complexity_score: number, audio_complexity_rating: string }`

## `get_control_bus_info`

*Read-only.*

Read a USoundControlBus asset and its live value in the editor world without changing anything. default_value is the bus default normalized value; current_value is what UAudioModulationStatics::GetModulatorValue returns for the bus in the editor world, and the engine answers 1.0 for a bus that is not active there, so 1.0 alone does not prove a mix is applied; with no editor world it equals default_value. subsystem_active says whether the editor world has an audio modulation manager. A bus that cannot be loaded is an error. Push a value with set_control_bus_value; mix stages: get_control_bus_mix_info; patches: get_sound_modulation_patch_info; parameters and generators: get_modulation_parameter_info, get_modulation_generator_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bus_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the USoundControlBus, e.g. "/Game/Audio/Bus_Music.Bus_Music" |

**Returns:** `{ bus_path, default_value, current_value, subsystem_active }`

## `get_control_bus_mix_info`

*Read-only.*

Reads the stages of a USoundControlBusMix asset without changing it. Returns mix_path, stage_count and stages, one per stage with bus_path (empty when the bus reference is cleared), target_value, attack_time and release_time. Edit a stage with set_control_bus_mix_stage_value.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mix_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the USoundControlBusMix |

**Returns:** `{ mix_path, stage_count, stages: [{ bus_path, target_value, attack_time, release_time }] }`

## `get_metasound_info`

*Read-only.*

Read the top-level metadata of a MetaSound Source asset (a preset included), loading it if needed: its class, the root graph class name, the graph inputs and outputs (name and type) with their counts, interface_count (the number of interfaces the document declares) and the node, connection (edge) and variable counts of the root graph's default page; with include_defaults, each input's default value too. Read-only; a path that does not resolve to a UMetaSoundSource, a MetaSound Patch included, is an error. list_metasound_nodes lists the nodes; get_assets_by_type with asset_type MetaSoundSource finds sources. The edges themselves: list_metasound_connections.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the MetaSound Source, as a package path like "/Game/MetaSounds/MS_Example" or an object path like "/Game/MetaSounds/MS_Example.MS_Example" |
| `include_defaults` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default false). When true, each inputs[] entry gains value: its default as the MetaSound editor builder reads it (a literal string), or "(inherited)" when the builder has none (a preset input taken from its referenced asset). Opens the editor builder for the asset; the asset is not changed. |

**Returns:** `{ source_name: string, asset_path: string, class_name: string, graph_class_name: string, input_count: number, output_count: number, interface_count: number, node_count: number, connection_count: number, variable_count: number, inputs: [{ name: string, type: string, value?: string }], outputs: [{ name: string, type: string }] }`

## `get_metasound_node_info`

*Read-only.*

Read one node of the default graph of a MetaSound Source by GUID: its name, class name, input/output/environment vertices (name, type_name, vertex_id), each input's stored default literal (has_value, literal_type, value; has_value false means no literal is set), the input literal defaults by vertex, and the Configuration struct class; input_name narrows inputs and input_defaults to one input, and an unknown input name fails listing the valid ones. Read-only; get node ids from list_metasound_nodes, write an input default with set_metasound_node_input_default.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | MetaSound Source asset path, e.g. "/Game/Audio/MS_Rain"; MetaSound Patches are not accepted. |
| `node_id` | string | yes | Node GUID, as list_metasound_nodes returns it in id; a value that is not a GUID is refused. |
| `input_name` | string | no | Optional name of one input vertex (FMetasoundFrontendVertex::Name): inputs and input_defaults then hold only that input. A name the node has no input for is an error listing the inputs. |

**Returns:** `{ metasound_path, node_id, name, class_name, input_name?, inputs: [{name, type_name, vertex_id, has_value, literal_type?, value?}], outputs: [{name, type_name, vertex_id}], environment: [...], input_defaults: [{vertex_id, input_name, value, type}], configuration_class }`

## `get_metasound_node_property`

*Read-only.*

Read one field of the Configuration struct of a MetaSound Source node, found by its node GUID (from list_metasound_nodes), returning its C++ type, has_value and value as JSON. Use it because MetaSound nodes are document structs, not UObjects, so get_properties cannot reach them; input defaults are set_metasound_node_input_default. Fails when the node has no Configuration struct or no such property; Patches are refused. Read-only; write with set_metasound_node_property.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | MetaSound Source asset path, e.g. "/Game/Audio/MS_Rain"; MetaSound Patches are not accepted. |
| `node_id` | string | yes | Node GUID, as list_metasound_nodes returns it in id; a value that is not a GUID is refused. |
| `property` | string | yes | FProperty name on the Configuration struct. |

**Returns:** `{ metasound_path, node_id, property, type, has_value, value? }`

## `get_modulation_generator_info`

*Read-only.*

Read the class and settings of a USoundModulationGenerator asset without changing it. settings depend on the class: LFO gives shape, frequency, amplitude, offset and phase; ADEnvelope gives attack_time and decay_time; EnvelopeFollower gives attack_time, release_time, gain and audio_bus_path (empty when no audio bus is set); any other generator class gives an empty settings object. Use it to check create_modulation_generator or set_modulation_generator_settings; for a modulation parameter use get_modulation_parameter_info, for a control bus get_control_bus_info, for a patch get_sound_modulation_patch_info. A path that does not load as a modulation generator is an error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `generator_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the generator, e.g. "/Game/Audio/Mod/LFO_Wobble", as create_modulation_generator returns it. |

**Returns:** `{ generator_path, generator_class, settings: {...} }`

## `get_modulation_parameter_info`

*Read-only.*

Reads a USoundModulationParameter asset without changing it. Returns parameter_path, parameter_class (the concrete class, e.g. SoundModulationParameterVolume) and its settings value_normalized, clamp_to_normalized_range and value_unit. Change them with set_modulation_parameter_settings.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `parameter_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the USoundModulationParameter |

**Returns:** `{ parameter_path, parameter_class, value_normalized, clamp_to_normalized_range, value_unit }`

## `get_sound_class_properties`

*Read-only.*

Read a USoundClass asset: every FSoundClassProperties field that set_properties writes (volume, pitch, filters, reverb and routing flags, output_target, loading_behavior) plus its name and its direct parent and direct children by name and path. A flattened view under the snake_case keys that tool takes; get_properties reads the raw Properties struct or any other UPROPERTY. parent_class is "None" for a root class, and child_count is the number of children listed (null references are skipped). One level only: walk further by calling it again on a parent or child. Read-only; it loads the asset by object or package path, and one that does not load as a USoundClass is an error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sound_class_path` | string | yes | Content path of the USoundClass asset. |

**Returns:** `{ name: string, sound_class_path: string, volume: float, pitch: float, low_pass_frequency: float, attenuation_distance_scale: float, lfe_bleed: float, voice_center_channel_volume: float, radio_filter_volume: float, radio_filter_volume_threshold: float, default_2d_reverb_send_amount: float, apply_effects: bool, always_play: bool, is_ui_sound: bool, is_music: bool, center_channel_only: bool, apply_ambient_volumes: bool, reverb: bool, output_target: string, loading_behavior: string, parent_class: string, parent_class_path: string, child_classes: [{name, path}], child_count: int }`

## `get_sound_cue_graph`

*Read-only.*

Read the node graph of a USoundCue without changing it: every node in AllNodes with its id (the node_id other sound cue tools take), class, child_ids (-1 for an empty slot), max_child_nodes and editable properties, plus first_node_id (-1 when unset) and node_count.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cue_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the cue |

**Returns:** `{ cue_path: string, asset_path: string, nodes: [object], node_count: int, first_node_id: int, has_first_node: bool }`

## `get_sound_modulation_patch_info`

*Read-only.*

Read a USoundModulationPatch asset without changing it: bBypass (a bypassed patch outputs the default value of its output parameter), output_parameter with its path and class (null when none is set), and one inputs entry per input, in order, holding the bus path (empty when that input has no bus) and a name that is always empty because the engine input struct has no name. A patch that cannot be loaded is an error. Change it with set_modulation_patch_bypass, set_modulation_patch_output_parameter, add_modulation_input_to_patch and remove_modulation_input_from_patch; make one with create_sound_modulation_patch; read an input bus with get_control_bus_info and the output parameter with get_modulation_parameter_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `patch_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the USoundModulationPatch, e.g. "/Game/Audio/Patch_Duck.Patch_Duck" |

**Returns:** `{ patch_path, bBypass, output_parameter: { path, class } | null, inputs: [{ bus: { path }, name }], input_count }`

## `get_sound_source_bus`

*Read-only.*

Read the routing fields of a USoundSourceBus asset: source_bus_channels (Mono or Stereo), duration in seconds (0 plays indefinitely) and the UAudioBus it outputs to (audio_bus_path and audio_bus_class, empty when none). Read-only. Writer: set_sound_source_bus_audio_bus.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ssb_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the USoundSourceBus, e.g. "/Game/Audio/SSB_Radio". |

**Returns:** `{ ssb_path: string, asset_class: string, source_bus_channels: string, duration: float, audio_bus_path: string, audio_bus_class: string }`

## `get_soundfield_submix_info`

*Read-only.*

Read a USoundfieldSubmix asset without changing it: its soundfield_encoding_format and resolved_format, encoding_settings {class, path}, and effect_chain entries {index, class, path, settings_class, settings_path} with chain_length. Adds a note when no concrete soundfield effect class is loaded.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `submix_path` | string | yes | Full path to the USoundfieldSubmix (required). |

**Returns:** `{ submix_path, soundfield_encoding_format, resolved_format, encoding_settings_class, encoding_settings: { class, path }, effect_chain: [{ index, class, path, settings_class, settings_path }], chain_length, note? }`

## `get_submix_effect_chain`

*Read-only.*

Read the effect chain of a USoundSubmix asset in order: one entry per slot with the name, class and path of its USoundEffectSubmixPreset ("None" for an empty slot), plus chain_length. Read-only; add_submix_effect_to_chain appends to it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `submix_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the USoundSubmix, e.g. "/Game/Audio/SM_Master.SM_Master". |

**Returns:** `{ submix_path: string, effects: [object], chain_length: int }`

## `list_metasound_connections`

*Read-only.*

List every edge of the default graph of a MetaSound Source: from which node and output pin to which node and input pin, with each node's name and class (a graph input or output node is named after the input or output), plus count. Read-only. It reads what connect_metasound_nodes, connect_metasound_graph_input_to_node, connect_metasound_graph_input_to_output and connect_metasound_node_to_graph_output write; node ids are those of list_metasound_nodes, and an input's edge is dropped with disconnect_metasound_nodes. Patches are refused.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | MetaSound Source asset path, e.g. "/Game/Audio/MS_Rain". |

**Returns:** `{ metasound_path: string, count: int, connections: [{ from_node_id, from_node_name, from_node_class, from_output_name, to_node_id, to_node_name, to_node_class, to_input_name, data_type }] }`

## `list_metasound_node_types`

*Read-only.*

Enumerate all MetaSound node classes registered with the engine (via Metasound::Frontend::ISearchEngine). Editor-only because ISearchEngine::FindAllClasses is gated by WITH_EDITORONLY_DATA.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `include_unloaded` | boolean | no | If true (default), include classes from assets not yet loaded into memory. |

**Returns:** `{ count, types: [{ class_name, class_path, type, version, is_native }] }`

## `list_metasound_nodes`

*Read-only.*

List every node in the default graph of a MetaSound Source asset with its GUID id, name, class name and input/output counts, plus count. Read-only; pass the id to get_metasound_node_info and the other node tools.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | MetaSound Source asset path, e.g. "/Game/Audio/MS_Rain"; MetaSound Patches are not accepted. |

**Returns:** `{ metasound_path, count, nodes: [{ id, name, class_name, input_count, output_count }] }`

## `list_subtitle_cues`

*Read-only.*

Lists all subtitle cues on a USubtitleAssetUserData.  Read-only walk of the Subtitles array, returning cue_count, max_duration (from USubtitleAssetUserData::GetMaximumDuration), and per-cue fields (index, text, start_offset, duration, duration_type, priority, subtitle_type, comment).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_path` | string | yes | Content path of the USubtitleAssetUserData asset. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, success: bool, count: int, max_duration: float, cues: [{index, text, start_offset, duration, duration_type, priority, subtitle_type, comment}] }`

## `play_sound`

*Additive.*

Starts the sound already assigned to an audio component of the editor world, matched by object name (case-insensitive) against the first audio component of each actor; components in a running PIE world are not reached. start_time is an offset in seconds into the sound. A component without a sound is an error: assign one with set_audio_sound. Transient: nothing is saved, marked dirty or undoable. was_playing and playing are read just before and just after the call. Stop with stop_sound; to play an asset at a location without a component use play_sound_at_location.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio_component_name` | string | yes | Name of the audio component to play sound on |
| `start_time` | number | no | Optional offset in seconds to start playback at |

**Returns:** `{ audio_component_name: string, playing: bool, was_playing: bool, sound_name: string, start_time: number, success: bool }`

## `play_sound_at_location`

*Additive.*

Play a sound asset (sound wave, sound cue or MetaSound source) once at a world location in the editor world, as a fire-and-forget one-shot with no audio component (UGameplayStatics::PlaySoundAtLocation) and only the sound's own attenuation. Nothing is saved, dirtied or undoable, and no handle comes back: the sound plays to its end, a looping one keeps looping with no way to stop it from here, and one out of the listener's earshot is skipped by the engine. Each call starts another instance. success is true once the request is made, even with no audio device. A sound that does not load or a location that is not an array of 3 numbers is an error. For playback you can stop or inspect, use play_sound and stop_sound on an audio component (set_audio_sound assigns its sound).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sound_path` | string | yes | Object path of the sound asset, e.g. '/Game/Audio/MySound.MySound' (the package path '/Game/Audio/MySound' also loads). |
| `location` | array | yes | World position [x, y, z] in centimetres, e.g. [0, 0, 100]; required, and the origin [0, 0, 0] is valid. |
| `volume` | number | no | Optional volume multiplier, e.g. 0.5 for half; default 1.0. |
| `pitch` | number | no | Optional pitch multiplier, e.g. 2.0 for an octave up; default 1.0. |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees, the facing of the sound (it matters to a directional attenuation); default [0, 0, 0]. |

**Returns:** `{ sound_path: string, sound_name: string, location: { x, y, z }, rotation: { pitch, yaw, roll }, volume: number, pitch: number, success: bool }`

## `remove_bus_from_mix`

*Destructive.*

Removes every stage that uses a USoundControlBus from a USoundControlBusMix asset and saves the mix; a removal succeeds only when the mix reaches disk. A bus that is not in the mix is already the state asked for: the call succeeds with removed false and already_absent true, and saves nothing. Returns mix_path, bus_path, removed, already_absent, stage_count, saved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mix_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the USoundControlBusMix |
| `bus_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the USoundControlBus to remove from the mix |

**Returns:** `{ mix_path, bus_path, removed, already_absent, stage_count, saved }`

## `remove_metasound_graph_input`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Removes a graph INPUT (and its node) from a MetaSound Source by name (inverse of add_metasound_graph_input).  Queries GetGraphInputNames first: if the input is already absent it returns already_absent without error (idempotent), otherwise it calls UMetaSoundBuilderBase::RemoveGraphInput and reports the result. Saves the asset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the MetaSound Source. |
| `input_name` | string | yes | Name of the graph input to remove. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, input_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string?, note: string? }`

## `remove_metasound_graph_output`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Removes a graph OUTPUT (and its node) from a MetaSound Source by name (inverse of add_metasound_graph_output).  Queries GetGraphOutputNames first: if the output is already absent it returns already_absent without error (idempotent), otherwise it calls UMetaSoundBuilderBase::RemoveGraphOutput and reports the result. Saves the asset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the MetaSound Source. |
| `output_name` | string | yes | Name of the graph output to remove. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, output_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string?, note: string? }`

## `remove_metasound_interface`

*Destructive.*

Remove an interface from a MetaSound Source graph, with the graph inputs and outputs (and their nodes) it declared, in one undo step, then save the asset. Inverse of add_metasound_interface. The reply re-reads the document's interfaces (interface_count, still_declared). An interface the graph does not declare is an honest no-op (removed=false, nothing saved); a source that does not load is an error. Removing the source interface a one-shot MetaSound Source needs (UE.Source...) leaves a source the engine may refuse to play; get_metasound_info lists what is declared.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the MetaSound Source. |
| `interface_name` | string | yes | Name of the declared interface to remove, as add_metasound_interface took it. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, interface_name: string, removed: bool, still_declared: bool, interface_count: int, saved: bool, save_error: string?, note: string? }`

## `remove_metasound_node`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Removes a node from a MetaSound Source graph by its node_id GUID (inverse of add_metasound_node).  Parses the node_id into a node handle and queries ContainsNode first: if the node is already absent it returns already_absent without error (idempotent), otherwise it calls UMetaSoundBuilderBase::RemoveNode (pruning unused dependencies) and reports the result. Saves the asset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metasound_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the MetaSound Source. |
| `node_id` | string | yes | GUID of the node to remove (from add_metasound_node). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, node_id: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string?, note: string? }`

## `remove_modulation_input_from_patch`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove every input of a USoundModulationPatch asset whose control bus has the same asset name as the bus at bus_path (so a same-named bus in another folder matches too), then save the patch; undo does not restore it. Inverse of add_modulation_input_to_patch; list the inputs first with get_sound_modulation_patch_info. Idempotent: when no input matches, nothing is changed or saved and the call succeeds with removed false and already_removed true. A patch or bus that does not load is an error and nothing changes; a removal succeeds only when the patch reaches disk, so a failed save (for example while PIE runs) makes success false with the inputs gone only in memory. input_count is the number of inputs left.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `patch_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the USoundModulationPatch, e.g. "/Game/Audio/Mod/MP_Volume", as create_sound_modulation_patch returns it. |
| `bus_path` | string | yes | Asset path of an existing USoundControlBus, e.g. "/Game/Audio/Mod/CB_Music"; it must load, and only its asset name is compared with the inputs' buses. |

**Returns:** `{ patch_path, bus_path, removed, already_removed, input_count, saved }`

## `remove_sound_cue_node`

*Destructive.*

Delete one node from a USoundCue asset, in one undo step, then save the cue. Inverse of add_sound_cue_node: every input slot that held the node is emptied (slots are kept, as disconnect_sound_cue_nodes keeps them), the cue output (FirstNode) is cleared when it was this node, the node leaves AllNodes, and its node in the cue editor's graph goes too when the cue has one. node_id is an index into AllNodes, so the nodes after it move down by one: id_remap lists {old_id, new_id} for each, and the ids from earlier calls are stale. A cue that does not load or a node_id out of range is an error and nothing changes. A failed save, as during PIE, makes success false with save_error. Read back: get_sound_cue_graph.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cue_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the cue |
| `node_id` | number | yes | node_id of the node to delete (its index in the cue AllNodes, from add_sound_cue_node or get_sound_cue_graph) |

**Returns:** `{ cue_path: string, node_id: int, node_class: string, removed: bool, slots_cleared: int, first_node_cleared: bool, graph_node_removed: bool, id_remap: [{old_id, new_id}], node_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `remove_sound_mix_class_override`

*Destructive.*

Remove the sound class adjuster for one sound class from a USoundMix, in one undo step, then save the mix. Inverse of set_sound_mix_class_override, which adds or updates that adjuster. A mix with no adjuster for the class is an honest no-op (removed=false, nothing saved); a mix or class that does not load is an error. The reply re-reads the mix's adjusters (remaining_classes). A failed save makes success false with save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sound_mix_path` | string | yes | Content path of the USoundMix asset. |
| `sound_class_path` | string | yes | Content path of the USoundClass whose adjuster to remove. |

**Returns:** `{ sound_mix_path: string, sound_class_path: string, removed: bool, removed_count: int, total_adjusters: int, remaining_classes: [string], saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `remove_soundfield_effect`

*Destructive.*

Detach the effect at effect_index from a USoundfieldSubmix effect chain (undoable) and save; the effect object stays in the package, an out-of-range index is an error, and a removal succeeds only when the submix reaches disk. Returns removed_effect_class, removed_effect_path and chain_length. With no concrete effect class loaded nothing changes and the call fails, with removed false and a note.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `submix_path` | string | yes | Full path to the USoundfieldSubmix (required). |
| `effect_index` | number | yes | Zero-based index into SoundfieldEffectChain (required). |

**Returns:** `{ submix_path, effect_index, removed_effect_class, removed_effect_path, removed: true, already_absent: false, chain_length, saved, save_error? } -- success only when saved; with no concrete effect class loaded the call fails with { submix_path, effect_index, removed: false, saved: false, note } and the chain is not touched.`

## `remove_submix_effect_from_chain`

*Destructive.*

Remove the entry at effect_index from a USoundSubmix's effect chain, in one undo step, notify the submix of the edit (as the Details panel does, so a running audio device rebuilds the chain) and save the submix. Inverse of add_submix_effect_to_chain; the later entries move up one index. The preset itself is not deleted: a preset add_submix_effect_to_chain made inside the submix package stays in it unreferenced, one appended by path stays where it was. An index out of range or a submix that does not load is an error and nothing changes; a failed save makes success false with save_error. Read the chain first with get_submix_effect_chain; a soundfield submix's effects: remove_soundfield_effect.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `submix_path` | string | yes | Full content path of the target USoundSubmix |
| `effect_index` | number | yes | 0-based position in the chain, as get_submix_effect_chain lists it |

**Returns:** `{ submix_path: string, effect_index: int, removed_effect: string, removed_effect_class: string, removed: bool, chain_length: int, chain: [string], saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `remove_subtitle_cue`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove a single FSubtitleAssetData cue by index. Inverse of add_subtitle_cue; use delete_asset to destroy the whole asset instead. Idempotent: an out-of-range index returns removed:false + note, not an error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_path` | string | yes | /Game path to the USubtitleAssetUserData. |
| `cue_index` | number | yes | 0-based index into Subtitles[]. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, cue_index, removed, previous_count, new_count }`

## `set_audio_3d_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Apply a 3D audio preset to one audio component of a placed actor in the editor world, in one undo step that dirties the level without saving it: spatialization (bAllowSpatialization) plus, for every preset but Disabled, an attenuation override sphere with the preset's inner radius and falloff distance (High 1000/2000 cm, Enabled and Medium 500/1000, Low 250/500); Disabled turns both off. audio_3d_configured is read back from the component; attenuation_falloff and the cone numbers only describe the preset. The same preset again gives the same result. Only the first audio component of each actor is searched, by object name; a missing component or unknown preset is an error and nothing changes. Read the result with get_audio_component_properties; set_audio_volume and set_audio_sound change the rest.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio_component_name` | string | yes | Object name of the audio component, compared without case against the first audio component of each actor, e.g. 'AudioComponent0' (get_audio_settings lists them). |
| `audio_3d_settings` | string | yes | Preset name: 'Enabled', 'Disabled', 'High', 'Medium' or 'Low' (case-insensitive); any other name is an error. |

**Returns:** `{ audio_component_name: string, audio_3d_settings: string, audio_3d_configured: bool, audio_3d_message: string, old_3d_enabled: bool, new_3d_enabled: bool, attenuation_override: bool, applied_attenuation_radius?: number, applied_falloff_distance?: number, 3d_enabled: bool, spatialization_enabled: bool, attenuation_distance: number, attenuation_radius: number, attenuation_falloff: number, attenuation_cone_angle: number, attenuation_cone_feather: number, audio_3d_recommendations: [string] }`

## `set_audio_bus_channels`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Change the channel layout (AudioBusChannels) of an existing UAudioBus asset and save it; success requires the save. Returns channels, channels_int and num_channels read back from the asset. To make a new bus use create_audio_bus.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bus_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAudioBus, e.g. "/Game/Audio/AB_Music". |
| `channels` | string | yes | EAudioBusChannels: 'Mono' \| 'Stereo' \| 'Quad' \| 'FiveDotOne' \| 'SevenDotOne', case-insensitive; FivePointOne, 5.1, SevenPointOne and 7.1 are accepted too. |

**Returns:** `{ bus_path: string, asset_class: string, channels: string, channels_int: int, num_channels: int, saved: bool }`

## `set_audio_sound`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Sets the sound asset of an audio component of the editor world, matched by object name (case-insensitive) against the first audio component of each actor; components in a running PIE world are not reached. A component that is playing restarts with the new sound unless it allows multiple instances. The change is not saved, marked dirty or undoable. A missing component or a sound that does not load is an error. previous_sound_name names the sound it replaced (None when there was none). Start playback with play_sound.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio_component_name` | string | yes | Name of the audio component to modify |
| `sound_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the sound (e.g. '/Game/Audio/MySound.MySound') |

**Returns:** `{ audio_component_name: string, sound_path: string, sound_name: string, previous_sound_name: string, sound_duration: number, success: bool }`

## `set_audio_volume`

*Destructive, idempotent.*
